questions: Where does the curve level off, and what is that level called?
How is the early part of the curve different from its later part?
segments.say: The logistic curve bends to the ceiling. The population grows almost exponentially at first, but as it nears the carrying capacity K the growth slows, the curve bends over and levels exactly at P = K. Point at the dashed ceiling line on your student notes diagram before any slope-field work starts.

questions: Where are the slope ticks steepest, and where are they flattest?
Where does a population starting above K end up, and why?
segments.say: A slope field funnels all starts to K. The slope ticks are steep for small populations and flatten near K, so low, middle and high starting curves are all funnelled to the same carrying-capacity equilibrium. Now try the settle-point questions on your worksheet.

questions: Why does the growth rate peak halfway to K rather than at K?
What is the growth rate at P = K, and what does that mean for the curve?
segments.say: The equation behind the bend. In dP/dt = rP(1 - P/K) the factor (1 - P/K) brakes the growth: the rate rises, peaks halfway to K, then falls to zero at P = K. Check the rate curve against your student notes before moving on.

questions: Why can the population no longer settle at the old K once harvesting starts?
Where does the population settle after harvesting, compared with before?
segments.say: Harvesting drags the equilibrium down. Steady harvesting removes population every season, so the old ceiling no longer balances: the equilibrium line drops and the population re-settles at the lower ceiling. Keep the bending-to-K order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
segments.watchFor: The population keeps growing faster and faster like a pure exponential, so it never slows down or levels off. Listen for students who extrapolate the early steep rise straight through the ceiling. Send them back to scene 1 and scene 3: As the population nears the carrying capacity K the growth rate falls to zero, so the curve bends over and levels at P = K, the stable equilibrium every starting population is funnelled to.
